title: Atomistic Visualization of Metal-support Interaction Assisted Sintering Dynamics
content: Sintering is a well-established deactivation pathway in heterogeneous catalysis, significantly influencing both catalytic activity and selectivity. A fundamental understanding of this phenomenon is crucial for the design of next-generation catalysts capable of maintaining long-term stability in industrial applications. Conventionally, sintering dynamics are described by two well-accepted mechanisms [1]: Ostwald ripening (OR) and particle migration and coalescence (PMC). OR involves the migration of atomic species across the vacuum or support, while PMC is driven by the Brownian-like motion of particles. However, these two classical models predominantly assume that the oxide supports are inert and often overlook the critical role of metal-support interactions on sintering dynamics under reactive conditions. To investigate the sintering dynamics of heterogenous catalysts under reactive conditions, our attention is directed towards the dynamic behaviors of Rh/TiO2 under different reactive conditions. Using environmental transmission electron microscope (ETEM), we reveal a metal-support interaction-promoting sintering processes in O2, where TiO2 undergoes reconstruction, facilitated by the dissolution and extraction of Rh into the TiO2 support. By contrast, partially reduced TiO2 support in vacuum at high temperatures stabilizes Rh NPs on the surface without particle migration.
